## 1- FsEpi Seurat input and MEL target genes

```{r}
##> Based on "Cell_states"-> BAS/FIB/GRN/SPN
load("R11_3_split_obj_for_Exfinder.Rdata")
      # Fib_obj, FsEpi_obj, PmtHEE_obj 
DefaultAssay(FsEpi_obj) <- "RNA"
Idents(FsEpi_obj)="Cell_states" # BAS/SPN/GRN/MEL

markers_celltype <- FindAllMarkers(FsEpi_obj, 
                                   only.pos = TRUE, 
                                   min.pct = 0.25, 
                                   logfc.threshold = 0.25,
                                   test.use = "wilcox")

## extract top10 genes
markers_celltype %>%group_by(cluster) %>%top_n(n = 10, wt = avg_log2FC) -> top10_marker_genes_FsEpi

## save it in list() for eahc cluster,create a list where each element is a vector of genes for each cluster
top10_marker_list_FsEpi <- split(top10_marker_genes_FsEpi$gene, top10_marker_genes_FsEpi$cluster)
```

```{r}
## plot
# scale the data
all.genes <- rownames(FsEpi_obj)
FsEpi_obj <- ScaleData(FsEpi_obj, 
                     features = all.genes)

top10<- top10_marker_genes_FsEpi$gene

p1<-DoHeatmap(FsEpi_obj, 
          features = top10) + 
          NoLegend() +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = c("#377EB8", "white", "#E41A1C"))
#> Scale for fill is already present.
#> Adding another scale for fill, which will replace the existing scale.
#> 
#> 
ggsave(p1,filename = "R17_1_top10_heatmap_FsEpi.pdf",
       width = 10, height =10)
```

## 2- Load exFINDER database

```{r}
# load exFINDER database
load("exFinder_data/LR_layer1_human.rda")
load("exFinder_data/RTF_layer2_human.rda")
load("exFinder_data/TFT_layer3_human.rda")

exFINDER.H <- list()
exFINDER.H[[1]] <- LR_layer1_human
exFINDER.H[[2]] <- RTF_layer2_human
exFINDER.H[[3]] <- TFT_layer3_human
```

## 3- Prepare the inputs for exFINDER analysis

-   for external signal,

    -   MEL-only

    -   or environment, or unknown cells [not present from all cells]

```{r}
# define the obj
selected_obj <- FsEpi_obj

# defien the factor
selected_obj$Type <- as.factor(selected_obj$Cell_states) # add "Type", very improtant for later analysis

#> [MEL-only] dataset of Fib-only cells for intersted ligand-expressing cells
cell_id <- subset(selected_obj@meta.data, 
                  Cell_states %in% c("MEL")) # 986 cells
mel_only_cells <- subset(selected_obj, cells=row.names(cell_id))

exp.data2 <- mel_only_cells@assays$RNA@data
meta.data2 <- mel_only_cells@meta.data ## need column ""Type" for cell labels


#> [All cells] the complete dataset contains all cells, which used for "external signals" from unknown cells or environment.
exp.Exdata <- selected_obj@assays$RNA@data
meta.Exdata <- selected_obj@meta.data
```

### 3.1- Calculate the threshold for each cell states

-   check the threshold for low and high expressed genes
-   MEL as target cells, higher threshold is 0.5, lowere threshold is 0.03.

```{r}
## calculate the percentile values of cell groups for determining the cutoff thresholds for “barely expressed genes” and “highly expressed genes” in later analysis
data <- get_percentile(Exp.Data = exp.Exdata,
               Meta.Data = meta.Exdata,
               percentile = c(.5, .75, .90))

p1<-ggplot(data=data, aes(x=Type, 
                      y=Ave.Exp., 
                      color=Prob.)) +
  geom_point(size=3) +
  theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5))

##
ggsave(p1,filename = "R12_6.1_threshold_check_FsEpi.pdf",
       width = 5, height =4)

## For MEL as target cells, lowly expressed threshold is lower than 0.5
## highly expressed threshold is higher than 0.9 for each cell group.
## Next, we mark those lowly expressed ligands among all cell groups as potential external signals.
```

![](images/Screenshot%202025-04-09%20at%2011.58.27%E2%80%AFPM.png){width="430"}

## 4- [FsEpi] **Identify all external signals that come from NON-MEL cells targeting MEL cells**

-   Could be the ligands from KC or ENV or another cells.

-   ligand--target Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) = ltGRN

-   the external signal-target signaling network = (exSigNet)

-   MEL is target cells, need MEL marker genes.

```{r}
##> Setup target genes (From MEL) and infer ltGRN
##> using MEL marker genes
target.gene_MEL <- c(top10_marker_list_FsEpi$MEL)

##> infer ltGRN, using MEL as target cells
ltGRN_MEL <- get_ltGRN(Target = target.gene, DB = exFINDER.H)
  # we get all KC-relatd itGRNs now, as ref.
```

#### [save] KC target genes + ltGRN

```{r}
save(target.gene_MEL,ltGRN_MEL, file = "R17_4_MEL_target_genes_ltGRN.Rdata")
```

## 5 [KC+ Env Ligands, MEL as targets]

-   Find all ligands not expressed from MEL
-   target MEL as input

```{r}
##> Identify external signals and infer exSigNet
##> [MEL-only] used here. We are intersted in the ligands of Non-KC cells, here could be 
meta.data2$Type <- as.factor(meta.data2$Cell_states) # ## very important
      # must be "factor" for all cell types.

Pex <- get_potentialex(Graph = ltGRN_MEL,
                Exp.Data = exp.data2,
                Meta.Data = meta.data2,
                cutoff = -0.03, # new lower threshold 
                AG.L = NULL)
## we found 663 ligands not expressed in KC
head(Pex)
#> "INHBE"   "ITGAM"   "ITGA4"   "ITGA9"   "NECTIN1" "JAM2" 

```

-   We have KC-ltGRN, and external Ligands, next, check the R/TF and target genes on Target cells t infer exSigNet. define the high threshold....
-   lexternal ligand in KC [low], R/TF/Target shoiuld be high in KC

```{r}
# [MEL-ONLY
##> 
exSigNet <- get_exSigNet(Graph = ltGRN_MEL,
                       Ligands = Pex, # the ligands must be potential external signals
                       Exp.Data = exp.data2,
                       Meta.Data = meta.data2,
                       par.cutoff = c(0.5, 0.5), #  two threshold for Receptor and TF.
                       # we select the receptors that are highly expressed in the KC
                       AG.R = c("MEL"),  
                       # we select the receptors that are highly expressed in the KC
                       AG.TF = c('MEL'))

## remove the overlap found.
exSigNet <- fix_OverLap(exSigNet)
# #> [1] "No overlap found!"

# check details
get_NetworkDetail(exSigNet) # show the details of exSigNet
  # Number of ligands:  119 
  # Number of receptors:  20 
  # Number of tfs:  60 
  # Number of targets:  10 
  # Number of L-R pairs:  156 
  # Number of R-TF pairs:  165 
  # Number of TF-T pairs:  184 
```

-   Check the ligand expression in all cells, MEL should be very low

```{r}
# [All-cells] check the external ligands and their expressions via heatmap
exS <- exSigNet$Graph.Node$Gene[exSigNet$Graph.Node$Role == "Ligand"]

p1<-get_heatmap(Gene = exS,
            Exp.Data = exp.Exdata,
            Meta.Data = meta.Exdata,
            cellwidth = 20,
            cellheight = 10,
            fontsize_row = 5,
             cluster_rows = TRUE)

ggsave(p1,filename = "R17_5_heatmap_ligand_check_MEL_target_FsEpi.pdf",
       width = 10, height =20)

exSigNet -> exSigNet.orig # for next
```

![](images/Screenshot%202025-04-21%20at%205.54.02%E2%80%AFPM.png){width="159"}

### 5.1 [BAS exSigNet -\> MEL as target]

-   Identify the exSigNet from BAS

-   using the highly expressed gene thresholds

```{r}
# select the external signals that expressed by BAS cells and infer the corresponding exSigNet
exSigNet <- get_exSigNetExData(Graph = exSigNet.orig,
                                 Exp.ExData = exp.Exdata,
                                 Meta.ExData = meta.Exdata,
                                 cutoff.ExData = 0.5,
                                 # find the external signals that are highly expressed in the BAS
                                 AG.ExData = c('BAS')) # define which Cell ligands you want to see. 

#####>>>>>>>>>>>>>>.>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
## if overlap found, we shoud fix it by.
## exSigNet <- fix_OverLap(exSigNet)

# #> [1] "No overlap found!"
# What does “overlap” mean in this context?
# In an external signaling network (exSigNet), you usually have a directed graph showing signaling from source nodes (e.g., ligands or upstream regulators) to target nodes (e.g., DEGs or downstream transcription factors).
```

-   calculate expression levels of the genes(nodes) in MEL, and predict signaling strength(weight).

```{r}
# calculate the expression levels in MEL, WE ARE intersted only in KC, so still use KC data for target.
exSigNet <- get_NodeValue(Graph = exSigNet,
                          Exp.Data = exp.data2, ## target cell MEL
                          Meta.Data = meta.data2, ## target cell MEL
                          AG.R = c("MEL"),
                          AG.TF = c('MEL'), #
                          AG.T = c('MEL'), # Target genes
                          Exp.ExData = exp.Exdata,
                          Meta.ExData = meta.Exdata,
                          # the expression of external signals are calculated using the data of MEL
                          AG.ExData = c('BAS'))

# predict signaling strengths (the default value of Kh is 2)
exSigNet <- get_EdgeWeight(Graph = exSigNet, 
               Kh = 2)
```

#### [Visualize for BAS ligands] heatmap

```{r}
# prepare the dataframe for heatmap plot [BAS ligand-target network]
exS_exp <- get_AveExp(Gene = exSigNet$Graph.Node$Gene,
           Exp.Data = exp.Exdata, # all cells
           Meta.Data = meta.Exdata)  # all cells

exS_exp.HP <- exS_exp
exS_exp.HP <- exS_exp.HP[, -1]
row.names(exS_exp.HP) <- exS_exp$Gene

# make data.frame includes all cell states
exS_exp.HP <- data.frame("BAS" = exS_exp.HP$BAS,
                     "SPN" = exS_exp.HP$SPN, 
                     'GRN' = exS_exp.HP$GRN,
                     "MEL" = exS_exp.HP$MEL)

row.names(exS_exp.HP) <- exS_exp$Gene

# [annotation col] customize the row labels and col labels
annotation_col = data.frame(
  CellType = c("KC", "KC", "KC", "MEL"))
rownames(annotation_col) = colnames(exS_exp.HP)

## ready for plot
annotation_row <- data.frame(Role = exSigNet$Graph.Node$Role)
row.names(annotation_row) <- row.names(exS_exp.HP)
```

-   plot

```{r}
# heatmap plot
bk <- c(seq(0,1.99,by=0.01), seq(2,4.5,by=0.01))

role_colors <- c(
  "Ligand" = "#FF89FF", 
  "Receptor" = "#FF9288",  
  "TF" = "#01D65C",  
  "Target" = "#82B7FF"   # pink
)

annotation_colors <- list(Role = role_colors,
                          CellType =c("KC"= "#BEC100",
                                       "MEL" = "#04DAE0"))


p <- pheatmap(exS_exp.HP, # modify the gene list can modify the heatmap
         cluster_row = FALSE, 
         cluster_cols = FALSE, 
         cellwidth = 12, 
         cellheight = 12,
         # gaps_row = c(1, 2, 6),
         fontsize_row = 10,
         fontsize_col = 10,
         annotation_row = annotation_row,
         annotation_col = annotation_col,
         annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
         color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(n = 7, name ="RdYlBu")))(length(bk)),
         breaks=bk)

ggsave(p,filename = "R17_5.1_heatmap_exSigNet_for_BAS_to_MEL_FsEpi.pdf",
       width = 10, height =10)
```

#### **[Visualize for BAS ligands] hierarchy plot**

```{r}
#>>>>  hierarchy plot
# after remove the duplicates in "gene" column in exSigNet$Graph.Node, error disappeared.
exSigNet_plot <- get_readyforplot(Graph = exSigNet)
```

```{r}
p <- ggraph(exSigNet_plot[[1]], layout = 'dendrogram', circular = TRUE) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(filter = leaf, x=x, y=y, colour=Role, size=Expression)) +
  theme_void() +
  geom_conn_bundle(data = get_con(from = exSigNet_plot[[2]]$from, 
                                  to = exSigNet_plot[[2]]$to, 
                                  Strength = exSigNet_plot[[2]]$weight), 
                   width = 1.0, aes(colour=Strength), 
                   arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, 'mm')), start_cap = circle(3, 'mm'), end_cap = circle(3, 'mm')) +
  scale_edge_color_continuous(low="#80b1d3", high="#FF7F24")+
  geom_node_text(aes(label = node)) +
  scale_size_continuous( range = c(0.1,10) )

ggsave(p,filename = "R17_5.1_hiplot_exSigNet_for_BAS_FsEpi.pdf",
       width = 12, height =10)
```

#### **[Visualize for BAS ligands] hive plot**

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(igraph)

## preapre for plot
Graph <- exSigNet

Role <- factor(x = Graph$Graph.Node$Role, levels = c("Ligand", "Receptor", "TF", "Target"))

edges <- data.frame("from" = Graph$Graph.Edge$from, "to" = Graph$Graph.Edge$to)

edges <- edges %>%
  mutate(weight = Graph$Graph.Edge$Weight)

nodes <- data.frame(name = Graph$Graph.Node$Gene, role = Role, value = Graph$Graph.Node$Size)

g2 <- graph_from_data_frame(vertices = nodes, d = edges)
```

```{r}
p<- ggraph(g2, 'hive', axis = nodes$role) + 
  geom_edge_hive(aes(colour = weight), width = 0.7, 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, 'mm')), 
                 start_cap = circle(3, 'mm'), 
                 end_cap = circle(3, 'mm')) + 
  # geom_axis_hive(aes(colour = role), size = 0, label = FALSE) + 
  geom_node_point(aes(size = value, color = role),  alpha = 1) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), angle = 45,  size = 6, repel = TRUE) +
  coord_fixed() +
  scale_edge_color_continuous(low="#80b1d3", high="#FF7F24") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks =element_blank(),
    axis.text =element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  ) 

# save
ggsave(p,filename = "R17_5.1_hiveplot_exSigNet_for_BAS_FsEpi.pdf",
       width = 12, height =10)
```

![](images/Screenshot%202025-04-21%20at%206.24.31%E2%80%AFPM.png){width="353"}

#### [Visual for BAS ligands] topo plot

```{r}
library(igraph)
library(RColorBrewer)

Graph <- exSigNet

# assigne the target cell colors
# Graph$Graph.Node$Role[Graph$Graph.Node$Gene %in% c("KRTDAP", "DMKN", "KRT14","KRT15","KRT5","KRT10","CALML5","CSTA","SPRR1B","KRT1","FABP7")] = "Selected Target" # define the color for target 1

actors <- data.frame(
  name = Graph$Graph.Node$Gene,
  role = Graph$Graph.Node$Role
)

relations <- data.frame(
  from = Graph$Graph.Edge$from,
  to = Graph$Graph.Edge$to
)

g <- graph_from_data_frame(
  relations, directed = TRUE,
  vertices = actors
)

l <- layout_with_gem(g) 

coul  <- brewer.pal(5, "Set2") 
# Create a vector of color
my_color <- coul[as.numeric(as.factor(V(g)$role))]

# save
pdf("R17_5.1_topo_exSigNet_for_BAS_FsEpi.pdf", 
    width = 15, height = 15)
plot(g, layout=l, vertex.color=my_color)
```
